Judgment

The above writ petition (Crl) is filed with following prayers :
"a. issue a writ of certiorari or other appropriate writ, direction or order calling for the records leading to Ext.P4 & Ext.P5 and quash the same and all proceedings there to as illegal and unconstitutional.
b. issue other appropriate writ order or direction as the case may be, in the entire facts and circumstances of the case."

[sic]

sentences.text: In Ext.P1 analyst report, the only defect was that the sample contained extraneous matter (iron filings) above the permissible limit is the submission.

In Ext.P6,
the referral laboratory reversed the said finding is the submission.
Therefore, there is divergent finding in the analyst report and the report of the referral laboratory.

Therefore, in the light of the dictum laid down by this Court in Pepsico India Holdings Private Limited v. State of Kerala and anr.
[2024(6) KHC 251], the proceedings is unsustainable, is the submission.
3.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings Private Limited v. State of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the Public Prosecutor.
4. This Court directed the Public Prosecutor to verify whether the point raised in this writ petition is covered by the judgment in Pepsico India's case (supra).
After going through the judgment, the Public Prosecutor fairly conceded that the point is covered by the above judgment.

This Court in Pepsico India's case (supra) observed like this :
WP(C) NO. 1260 OF 2021 2025:KER:37071 "15.

From the above, it is clear that, if the Designated Officer on obtaining the report of the Food Analyst is of the opinion for reason to be recorded in writing, that the report delivered by the Food Analyst under R.2.4.2 (5) is erroneous, he can forward one of the parts of the sample kept by him to referral laboratory, for analysis and if the analyst report of such referral laboratory is to the effect that the article of food is unsafe or substandard or mis - branded or containing extraneous matter, the provisions of R.3.1 shall, so far as may be, apply.
Hence, if the Designated Officer is of the opinion that the report delivered by the Food Analyst is erroneous, he can forward one part of the sample to the referral laboratory and even if the report of the referral laboratory is divergent from the report of the Food Analyst, the provisions of R.3.1 is applicable.

But on the other hand, if the report of the Food Analyst is challenged by way of appeal under S.46 (4)
of the FSS Act by the persons mentioned in R.3.1.1: (1) and the report of the referral laboratory confirmed the report of the Food Analyst, then only the prosecution steps can be initiated.
In other words, if the referral laboratory report is divergent from the report of the Food Analyst instead of confirming the report of the food analyst, no prosecution is possible.
Such a rule may be framed for the reason that, there is no further appeal to the accused to challenge the report of the referral laboratory, if it is divergent from the report of the Food analyst.

I am of the considered opinion that,
there is a lacuna in the rules.
It is true that in R.2.4.6: (1), it is stated that, 'the report of the referral laboratory shall be final in this regard'.

The word used is "final"
WP(C) NO. 1260 OF 2021 2025:KER:37071 and not "supersede".
Now, it will be useful to consider S.13(3) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
It says that, Certificate given by the Director of the Central Food Laboratory shall supersede the report given by the Public analyst.
Such a provision is not there in the FSS Act.
The words "final" and "supersede" have different meanings.
The word "final" emphasizes completion or conclusiveness while "supersede" implies replacement. "

In such circumstances, in the light of the above dictum, the proceedings is unsustainable.
Therefore, the same can be quashed.

Therefore, this writ petition (crl) is allowed in the following manner :
1) All further proceedings in Ext.P5 are quashed.
